title: Savitri at the banyan
hookLine: a banyan wound with thread: how Savitri's story became a vrata, a vow kept with the body
carry: a vrata turns a story into a vow
last: TIME NEAR THE GOOD IS NEVER WASTED.

lines: ONE WOMAN, MORE THAN ONE READING.
cards: A banyan tree, its trunk wound round and round with thread. On a festival day called Vat Savitri, some married Hindu women fast, walk around a banyan and tie thread to it, asking for long lives for their husbands.

The tree doesn't come from the epic's telling; it comes from the way the story has been lived since. On our last day with her: how a story becomes a vow, and how one woman can be read more than one way.

teach.h: THE GREATNESS OF THE DEVOTED WIFE
teach.b: Start with where the epic puts her. The story sits in the Mahabharata's forest book, in a section whose title can be translated as the greatness of the devoted wife.
The sage Markandeya tells it because Yudhishthira has asked: has there ever been a woman as devoted as Draupadi?

His answer is Savitri, and his last word is that Draupadi, like Savitri, will save them all. So the frame is devotion, and some readers keep it: a wife whose faithfulness is strong enough to stop Death.
Others hear a woman of fierce will and a sharp mind, who chose her own husband, kept a hard truth alone for a year, and argued with Death on the road.
A modern poet, Aurobindo, read her as the divine word come down to free the soul from death. Now the teaching. Hinduism has a name for what happens at the banyan: a vrata, a vow.

teach.h: VRATA: A FAST, A PUJA, A STORY TOLD
teach.b: You choose a day, you fast or keep a rule, you do a puja, and you hear the story the vow belongs to, its vrat katha, told out loud. Hindus keep vratas for Shiva, for the Goddess, on Ekadashi, for the people they love.
On Vat Savitri, the story is Savitri's.

And Savitri kept one herself: before the day Death came, the epic says, she held a three-night vow, fasting and standing still like a post. The women at the tree are doing a smaller version of what she did.

teach.h: A VRATA TURNS A STORY INTO A VOW.
teach.b: That's the gift of a vrata in a busy life. Love that would stay a feeling becomes a day you keep, with an empty stomach and a thread in your hand.

how: On Vat Savitri, some married Hindu women fast, worship at a banyan tree, wind thread around its trunk and hear Savitri's story told, asking for long lives for their husbands; the day and customs differ by region.

o: a wife the epic praises only for her obedience
a woman whose story became a vrata at the banyan
a queen who planted the first banyan in Madra

games.q: how Savitri is told and kept — tap the pairs.
p: a vow: a fast or rule, kept with a puja
the story told aloud during the vow

s: the banyan tree comes from the epic's own telling
the tree comes from the festival and later custom, not from the epic's words.
in the epic, Savitri keeps a vow of her own before the day Death comes

a vrata is just skipping a meal
it's a chosen vow: a fast or rule, a puja, and the vow's story told aloud.

games.q: your aunt is keeping the Vat Savitri vrata and asks you to help. what turns her fast into a vrata?
o: the vow itself, the puja at the banyan, and hearing Savitri's story told.
buying new thread for the tree.
games.why: a vrata is a chosen vow: a fast or rule, a puja, and the vrat katha, the story it belongs to, told out loud.

practice: Bring to mind someone whose life you'd ask to be long, and hold their face for a moment.
Then, slowly, as if winding thread around a banyan, go round them in your mind, their morning, their work, their evening, their sleep, one slow circle for each breath.
If you pray, you can pray for them, the way the women at the tree do.

wordCard.voice: Savitri. Told as the greatness of a devoted wife, read by others as a woman of will, and kept each year in a vrata at a banyan wound with thread.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the princess's name, also the name of the verse to the sun god Savitr and of the festival Vat Savitri.

carryVoice: Your line: a vrata turns a story into a vow. Savitri's became a thread around a banyan. Rest well.
